OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-08-14'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only create-time flag. When true, the owner is allowed to share a
            household (same last name and address) with an existing owner; otherwise a
            create request colliding with an existing household is rejected with 409.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is
                the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global
                4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned at creation time.
              type: string
              example: 'FRA-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household id
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier assigned when an owner is created with
                'sharesHousehold' true, joining an existing owner that has the same
                last name and address. Owners of the same household share this value.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, shared the same firstName and lastName compared
                case-insensitively (excluding this owner). Assigned at creation time.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where
                YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'FRA-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:
              title: Membership tier
              description: >-
                The owner's membership tier: 'SILVER' when namesakeCount is 0 and an
                email is present, otherwise 'BRONZE'.

## Summary

The registration date now always resolves to a business day, and every value derived from it uses that adjusted date. I did this by adding a single resolution step to the `POST /api/owners` OfficeFloor pipeline whose result feeds both the daily-limit check and the entity build, so they can't diverge.

**New files**
- `BusinessDay.java` — helper: rolls a Saturday/Sunday forward to the next Monday (spec is weekend-only), weekdays unchanged.
- `ResolveRegistrationDate.java` — reads the request body (`@Val OwnerFieldsDto`), takes the supplied `registrationDate` or defaults to `LocalDate.now()`, rolls it through `BusinessDay`, and publishes the single effective date as `Out<LocalDate>`.

**Changed files**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted a `resolveRegistrationDate` step (under `transaction` governance) after `ensureCityCapacity` and before `ensureDailyCapacity`, so the adjusted date is available to every downstream step.
- `EnsureDailyCapacity.java` — now consumes the `@Val LocalDate` effective date instead of computing its own `LocalDate.now()`, counting existing owners per adjusted business day and reporting that date on the 429.
- `BuildOwner.java` — now sets the owner's `registrationDate` to the resolved adjusted date unconditionally (replacing the old "default only when null" logic), so a supplied weekend date is rolled forward too and the mapper's membership-number year segment (`getRegistrationDate().getYear() % 100`) uses the adjusted date.

This satisfies the three behavioural requirements: supplied weekend dates now roll forward (Cp07), derived values like the membership number's year segment use the adjusted date (Cp14), and the daily create-limit counts per adjusted business day (Cp19), with the default-date business-day invariant preserved (Cp20).
